# Node.js/Express API Exercises — 2026-07-24

## Exercise 1: RESTful CRUD API for a Notes Collection
**Difficulty:** ⭐⭐ Basic  
**Concepts:** Express app setup, routing, HTTP methods, JSON body parsing, route parameters

**Description:** Build a RESTful API for managing notes using Express.js. Each note has `id` (auto-generated), `title`, `content`, and `createdAt`. Store notes in memory (an array). Implement full CRUD: GET all, GET by id, POST new, PUT update, DELETE. Use `express.json()` middleware.

**Starter Code:**
```javascript
const express = require('express');
const app = express();
const PORT = 3000;

// Middleware
app.use(express.json());

// In-memory storage
let notes = [];
let nextId = 1;

// GET /notes — List all notes
app.get('/notes', (req, res) => {
    res.json(notes);
});

// GET /notes/:id — Get a specific note
app.get('/notes/:id', (req, res) => {
    const id = parseInt(req.params.id);
    // Your code: find note or return 404
});

// POST /notes — Create a new note
app.post('/notes', (req, res) => {
    const { title, content } = req.body;
    // Your code: validate, create note with id and createdAt, return 201
});

// PUT /notes/:id — Update a note
app.put('/notes/:id', (req, res) => {
    const id = parseInt(req.params.id);
    // Your code: find and update, or return 404
});

// DELETE /notes/:id — Delete a note
app.delete('/notes/:id', (req, res) => {
    const id = parseInt(req.params.id);
    // Your code: remove or return 404
});

app.listen(PORT, () => {
    console.log(`Server running on http://localhost:${PORT}`);
});
```

**Expected Learning:** `const app = express()`, `app.use(express.json())`, route handlers (`app.get`, `app.post`, etc.), `req.params`, `req.body`, `res.json()`, `res.status()`, `parseInt()`, `app.listen()`.

**Test with curl:**
```bash
curl -X POST http://localhost:3000/notes -H "Content-Type: application/json" -d '{"title":"Shopping List","content":"Milk, Eggs, Bread"}'
curl http://localhost:3000/notes
curl http://localhost:3000/notes/1
curl -X PUT http://localhost:3000/notes/1 -H "Content-Type: application/json" -d '{"title":"Updated List","content":"Milk, Eggs, Bread, Butter"}'
curl -X DELETE http://localhost:3000/notes/1
```

## Exercise 2: Middleware for Logging, Validation, and Error Handling
**Difficulty:** ⭐⭐ Basic  
**Concepts:** Custom middleware, error-handling middleware, request validation, Morgan (logging)

**Description:** Enhance the notes API with middleware: (1) Install and use `morgan` for request logging, (2) Create a custom `validateNote` middleware that validates request body has `title` (required, string) and `content` (optional, string), (3) Create an error-handling middleware that catches all errors and returns consistent JSON error responses, (4) Add a 404 catch-all middleware.

**Starter Code:**
```javascript
const express = require('express');
const morgan = require('morgan');  // npm install morgan
const app = express();

// 1. Logging middleware
app.use(morgan('dev'));  // Logs: METHOD /path STATUS RESPONSE_TIME
app.use(express.json());

let notes = [];
let nextId = 1;

// 2. Custom validation middleware
function validateNote(req, res, next) {
    const { title } = req.body;

    if (!title) {
        return res.status(400).json({ error: 'Title is required' });
    }

    // Your code: validate title is a string, check content if provided
    next();
}

// 3. Routes with validation
app.post('/notes', validateNote, (req, res) => {
    // Your code: create note
});

app.put('/notes/:id', validateNote, (req, res) => {
    // Your code: update note
});

// ... other routes

// 4. 404 catch-all (must be after all routes)
app.use((req, res, next) => {
    // Your code: return 404 JSON
});

// 5. Error-handling middleware (4 parameters)
app.use((err, req, res, next) => {
    console.error(err.stack);
    // Your code: return 500 JSON error
});

app.listen(3000, () => {
    console.log('Server on port 3000');
});
```

**Expected Learning:** `app.use()` for middleware, `next()` function, custom middleware patterns, `morgan` logging, error-handling middleware (4 params), middleware ordering, `res.status()`.

## Exercise 3: Query Filtering and Search with Route Handlers
**Difficulty:** ⭐⭐⭐ Basic  
**Concepts:** Query parameters (req.query), filtering, search, sorting, pagination, modular route files

**Description:** Create a more advanced notes API with search/filter capabilities organized into a separate router file. Features: `GET /notes?search=` (full-text search in title and content), `?sort=` (by title or createdAt), `?order=asc|desc`, `?page=` and `?limit=` (pagination with total count). Use `express.Router()` to organize routes in a separate file.

**Starter Code:**

**File: `routes/notes.js`**
```javascript
const express = require('express');
const router = express.Router();

let notes = [];
let nextId = 1;

// ... (include all CRUD routes from Exercise 1, adapted for router)

// GET /notes — List with filtering, search, sorting, pagination
router.get('/', (req, res) => {
    let { search, sort, order, page, limit } = req.query;
    order = order || 'asc';
    page = parseInt(page) || 1;
    limit = parseInt(limit) || 10;

    let result = [...notes];

    // Your search logic: filter by search term in title and content
    if (search) {
        const term = search.toLowerCase();
        result = result.filter(
            n => n.title.toLowerCase().includes(term) ||
                 n.content.toLowerCase().includes(term)
        );
    }

    // Your sort logic: sort by field and direction
    if (sort) {
        result.sort((a, b) => {
            // Compare sort fields
        });
        if (order === 'desc') result.reverse();
    }

    // Your pagination logic
    const total = result.length;
    const start = (page - 1) * limit;
    const paginated = result.slice(start, start + limit);

    res.json({
        total,
        page,
        limit,
        totalPages: Math.ceil(total / limit),
        notes: paginated
    });
});

module.exports = router;
```

**File: `app.js`**
```javascript
const express = require('express');
const morgan = require('morgan');
const notesRouter = require('./routes/notes');

const app = express();

app.use(morgan('dev'));
app.use(express.json());

app.use('/notes', notesRouter);  // Mount the router

// 404 handler
app.use((req, res) => {
    res.status(404).json({ error: 'Route not found' });
});

app.listen(3000);
```

**Test URLs:**
```
GET /notes?search=shopping
GET /notes?sort=createdAt&order=desc
GET /notes?page=2&limit=5
GET /notes?search=hello&sort=title&page=1&limit=10
```

**Expected Learning:** `express.Router()`, modular route organization, `req.query`, query parameter parsing, array `.filter()` and `.sort()`, pagination math (`slice()`), structured API responses, `module.exports`.
